expected.summary: Right after component move took R1 from (24, 12) to (26, 12) mm: Layout's Undo takes the move back as one step, and R1's position reads back at 24 mm.

rows.reason: doc undo always takes back one write; a board without a write of this tool to take back is refused, as the conflict row and the adapter's own refusal after the board was opened again show.

expected.summary: The session has no such document open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

A forward-annotation job on this board was stopped by ending its worker process (Task Manager) while it ran, so its outcome is unknown and its operation keeps the board locked until operation resolve: E_CONFLICT target_locked, and nothing is sent to Layout.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the board; nothing is sent to Layout.

While a pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Help > About. A dialog box over Layout, or a Layout that stops answering, is reported as the session blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a Layout that stops answering does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away after its Undo command was sent.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: The board holds unsaved changes of earlier rows, and component move has just taken R1 to (26, 12) mm again: the undo takes that move back as usual, and the receipt reports the document dirty.
Right after component move took R1 to (26, 12) mm, the undo puts it back at 24 mm and waits before its read-back; meanwhile R1 is moved 2 mm aside (--tamper), so x_mm reads back 26, not 24.
